recent_posts.title: Saying Goodbye
recent_posts.summary: Wing, a company focused on simplifying cloud application development with its programming language Winglang, has announced its closure. Despite a strong initial community response and over 100 contributors, the company found it challenging to convert this enthusiasm into a sustainable business. After exploring various directions in the cloud space over the past year, the founders decided to shut down the operation. They expressed gratitude to their supporters and reminisced about the journey.

recent_posts.title: Inflight Magazine no. 11
recent_posts.summary: The 11th issue of Wing Inflight Magazine shares updates on Winglang, an open-source programming language designed for cloud applications. Highlights include a new homepage, the Wing by Example page, the introduction of a new 'bytes' type, CORS configuration for cloud buckets, new intrinsic functions, and a command to generate API documentation using the Wing CLI. The issue also covers updates to the Wing console and new Wing libraries (winglibs) like @winglibs/email and @winglibs/dynamodb.

recent_posts.title: The road to Wing 1.0
recent_posts.summary: Wing aims to deliver a robust environment for cloud application development by providing a comprehensive CLI, versatile platforms, and a strong testing framework. The compiler supports features like static typing and interoperability with TypeScript libraries, while the standard library offers built-in utilities for common programming tasks. The Wing Console/Simulator enhances local development with observability and interactivity. Extensive documentation and examples aim to make Wing accessible to both application developers and platform engineers.

recent_posts.title: Inflight Magazine no. 10
recent_posts.summary: Wing Inflight Magazine's 10th issue introduces updates to Winglang, an open-source cloud-first programming language. Highlights include the Wing 1.0 roadmap with its focus on cloud application development, new language and console features, and breaking changes. Notable updates include the introduction of the 'cloud.Service' resource, internal access modifiers, AWS Lambda Layer API support, and enhancements to the Wing console. The issue also covers new wing libraries (winglibs) and encourages community participation on GitHub and Discord.

recent_posts.title: Ported to Cloud with Winglang (Part One)
recent_posts.summary: This post discusses the successful porting of the 'Blue Zone' application from Java to Winglang using the Hexagonal Architecture pattern. It highlights the benefits of this approach and the challenges faced during the migration process. The post also presents the folder structure, class diagrams, and cloud resources diagram of the application.

recent_posts.title: Building your own ChatGPT Graphical Client with NextJS and Wing
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to build an AI-powered Q&A bot using Next.js, Wing, and LangChain. Connect Wing to a Next.js app and process user's requests with LangChain.

recent_posts.title: Managing Winglang Libraries with AWS CodeArtifact
recent_posts.summary: This post discusses the use of AWS CodeArtifact for managing Winglang libraries, including the creation of a CodeArtifact Domain and Repository, configuring npm with the login command, and publishing custom libraries.

recent_posts.title: Building your own ChatGPT Graphical Client with NextJS and Wing
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to build and deploy a ChatGPT client using Wing and Next.js. Ensure control over your data by self-hosting and running the application locally or on your own cloud infrastructure.

recent_posts.title: In Search for Winglang Middleware Part Two
recent_posts.summary: This post explores Winglang's capability to handle both preflight and inflight logic in middleware, specifically focusing on the use of the Template Method Design Pattern. It highlights the benefits of this design pattern, including post-processing steps, reuse of common request-handling definitions, and specification of multiple configurations. However, it also acknowledges the limitations of maintaining a high number of templates. The post concludes with plans for future research on overcoming these limitations using Winglang's unique capabilities.

recent_posts.title: Inflight Magazine no. 9
recent_posts.summary: Wing is a new programming environment for the cloud that makes it easy for developers to build and test distributed systems. It supports pluggable platform providers and is familiar and friendly for developers coming from object-oriented backgrounds. Wing has made improvements to debugging with breakpoints, added support for multiple cloud providers, and introduced a visual cloud simulator. It also allows for the adding of UI to Wing classes and has new project templates available.
